chunks: Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim al-Bazzaz al-Asadi from Dawud ibn Farqad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who claims the Imamate while he is not an Imam, has associated a lie with Allah, His Messenger, and us.

key_terms.وَعَلَيْنَا: And upon us (referring to the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of falsely claiming the Imamate in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith serves as a foundational criterion for distinguishing legitimate religious authority from imposture during the Minor and Major Ghebah. It establishes that falsely claiming the Imamate constitutes a tripartite lie against Allah, the Prophet, and the Imams, thereby invalidating the claimant's spiritual and political legitimacy in Shia jurisprudence.
